In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new conjugated polymers that contain 2,3- and 2,6-dialkoxy-1,4-phenylenes and iptycene units, respectively.
the synthesis and characterization of novel poly(phenylenevinylene)s (PPVs), poly(phenyleneethynylene)s ( PPEs ), and poly(p-phenylene)s (PPPs).
the development of new polymeric materials for applications in the fields of opto-electronics, nonlinear optics, and photonic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2,3- versus 2,5-disubstituted phenylenes in the polymer main chain have a significant effect on the electronic properties of the polymers.
the blue-shift in absorption and emission spectra observed in the polymers containing 1,4-dialkoxy-substituted phenylenes is a consequence of their higher HOMO energy level.
the 2,3-substituted monomers are not only synthetically accessible but also provide a means to access new conjugated polymers with unique optical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the blue-shifted emission of the new polymers is a result of the presence of the 2,3-substituted dialkoxybenzoides, which are more electron-withdrawing than the 2,5-substituted analogues.

the 2,3-disubstitution pattern in these conjugated polymers is not as good at delocalizing the π-electron system, as compared to the 2,5-disubstitution pattern, and that the iptycene-containing polymers have a lower band gap than their benzene analogues.

the introduction of the 2,3-disubstituted arene moiety into the conjugated polymer backbones results in a significant blue shift of the emission spectra, and this is a general phenomenon for the polymers containing this moiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iptycene-containing conjugated polymers can be readily synthesized by palladium-catalysed cross-coupling.

the incorporation of 1,4-dialkoxy-2,3-benzenes into PPE and PPV structures results in a dramatic blue shift in the emission spectrum relative to the corresponding polymers that incorporate 2,5-diarylene units.
the 2,3-substitution pattern of the 1,4-phenylenediyl unit in the polymer backbone is an effective way to control the electronic structure of the polymer and, in turn, to tune the optical properties.
